official.title: Postdoc Mechanical Behavior of Biobased Adhesives for Fibre-reinforced Polymers
official.description_text:
Develop biobased adhesives that combine reliable bonding with on-demand debonding. As a postdoctoral researcher at TU Delft, you will investigate the interfacial behaviour, mechanical performance and durability of composite joints to advance sustainable repair and recycling strategies.
Job description
Carbon fibre-reinforced polymer (CRFP) composites are essential in many high-performance applications, but repairing, disassembling and recycling these materials remains challenging. Conventional epoxy-based adhesives can make these processes difficult, contributing to material waste and limiting circularity. At TU Delft, you will contribute to a research project developing renewable, biobased thermoplastic adhesives that can be debonded on demand using heat. The goal is to enable more sustainable joining and repair strategies while maintaining the mechanical performance and durability required during service.
Your research will focus on understanding how the adhesive–composite interface influences adhesion, joint strength and long-term performance. Through advanced experimental investigations, you will study how interfacial structure and bonding behaviour respond to thermal and mechanical loading. You will also investigate the durability of composite joints under weathering and creep conditions, estimate their service lifetime and identify the mechanisms responsible for degradation.
Your experimental findings will contribute to the development and optimisation of durable, thermally debondable adhesives. You will work closely with another researcher in the project who uses computational methods to investigate the underlying molecular-level mechanisms. By connecting experimental observations with computational insights, you will help establish the scientific understanding needed to design adhesives that combine reliable performance with controlled debonding.
Your responsibilities
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will:
Perform experiments to investigate adhesive–composite interfacial interactions, calculate adhesion energies, and characterise interfacial structure and wetting behaviour for different biobased adhesives.
Investigate the mechanical performance to evaluate the bond strength and identify failure modes of the adhesive–CFRP composite interface.
Assess the joints behavior and strength under thermal and mechanical loads to establish and guiding the optimization of the adhesive formulations.
Establish the degradation mechanisms caused by the combined influence of temperature, moisture and UV-radiation.
Collaborate closely with computational researchers and project partners to connect experimental observations with atomistic insights and support the development of durable and thermally debondable adhesives.
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations and future research proposals in sustainable composite joining, repair and recycling.
Your work environment
You will be part of
Team Amarante Böttger
at TU Delft, whose research includes the experimental characterisation of materials, interfaces and their properties. Strong collaboration with her
team at Avans University of Applied Science
is envisioned. Your project on biobased, thermally debondable adhesives for carbon fibre-reinforced polymer composites will build on the expertise in thermoplastics and interfaces to uncover the mechanisms governing adhesion, interfacial stability and mechanical performance. By combining experimental research with atomistic simulations, you will contribute to the rational design of sustainable adhesive systems that enable easier repair, joining and recycling of composite materials.
You will collaborate closely with
Team Dey
within the
Computational Materials Science
section at TU Delft providing advanced atomistic simulations with expertise in density functional theory molecular dynamics and machine-learning interatomic potentials.
Job requirements
We are looking for a selfmotivated researcher to uncover the mechanisms governing adhesive composite interfaces and advance characterisation approaches for the development of sustainable, thermally debondable adhesives. You are independent but also a good team player and are willing to cooperate closely with other researchers and our industry partners.
Furthermore, you meet the following requirements:
You hold a PhD degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, or a closely related discipline.
You have strong expertise in experimental materials characterisation techniques, particularly joint strength testing and chemical surface analysis. Experience in composite manufacturing and knowledge of thermoplastics and degradation mechanisms is an advantage.
You are eager to apply this knowledge to understand the adhesion mechanism, and behavior of biobased adhesive–composite systems.
You have a strong track record in scientific research, as evident from publications in peer-reviewed international journals and conference participation.
You have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Faculty Mechanical Engineering
From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems.
ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation.

Conditions of employment
Duration of contract is 2,5 years. Temporary.
A job of 36-40 hours per week.
Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities.
An excellent pension scheme via the ABP.
The possibility to compile an individual employment package every year.
Discount with health insurers on supplemental packages.
Flexible working week.
Every year, 232 leave hours (at 38 hours). You can also sell or buy additional leave hours via the individual choice budget.
Plenty of opportunities for education, training and courses.
Partially paid parental leave
Attention for working healthy and energetically with the vitality program.
Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit,
Coming to Delft Service
, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A
Dual Career Programme
is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.  .
Additional information
For more information about this vacancy, please contact
recruitment-ME@tudelft.nl
.
The expected start date is February 2027 but no later than May 15th 2027; contract duration is 2.5 years. You will receive an update on the outcome of your application in the week of 14th December 2026. The first interviews are scheduled for the week of 14th December, followed by a second interview round in the second week of January 2027.

30 November 2026
via the application button and upload the following documents:
A cover letter in which you describe your motivation and specific qualifications for this position (max 1 page).
A cover letter in which you describe your motivation and specific qualifications for this position (max 1 page)
Your CV

You can address your application to Dr. Amarante Böttger and Dr. Poulumi Dey.
Please note:
To protect your personal data, we only accept applications submitted via the ‘Apply’ button advertised under the vacancies on our website. Applications and additional information sent by email or through other channels, including unsolicited applications, will not be considered or responded to. This also applies to open applications.
As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about
knowledge security.
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in materials science focused on experimental characterisation of biobased thermoplastic adhesives for carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer composites, with emphasis on interfacial behaviour, mechanical performance, durability and degradation mechanisms under thermal and environmental loading.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap with human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, or collaborative systems. Position is in materials engineering and composite science; the researcher's domain is HCI and human-centred immersive systems.

methodological_fit.rationale: Experimental research methodology exists in profile (user studies, experimental design). However, this position requires advanced materials characterisation techniques (joint strength testing, chemical surface analysis, thermomechanical testing, weathering/creep assessment) which are entirely outside the researcher's evidence base. Requires PhD in Materials Science, Physics or Chemistry; researcher holds MSc in Creative Multimedia.

growth_value.rationale: Position would not close capability gaps aligned with target identity. Researcher needs to deepen: immersive systems design, spatial cognition measurement, collaborative interaction design, advanced statistics (mixed-effects modelling), and advanced research methods in HCI. This position offers none of these.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft is a target institution (priority_2 threshold), which carries institutional weight. However, position is in Mechanical Engineering, not HCI/design-science groups. No clear supervision pathway to target identity. Funding appears stable but project focus is orthogonal to researcher's trajectory.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry or closely related discipline; researcher holds MSc by Research in progress in Creative Multimedia. MSc completion by start date (Feb 2027) is possible but degree discipline mismatch is fundamental.
Requires strong expertise in experimental materials characterisation techniques not evidenced in profile.
Position explicitly excludes pure computer science or design backgrounds; researcher's foundation is multimedia and HCI.
